cases.title: A review offered and never answered, then the learner comes back in a new session: the review is offered again, no lesson, no demo

rubric.reason: In turn 2, the new session, the mentor offers the review again ("Want to do a quick review on this comp?"), builds it from the earlier work and how long ago ("About ten days ago you made Blink's Opacity snap"), and stops for the answer with no lesson, demo or intent question.

Blink's Opacity, the two held pairs and the demo holding the first all come from the record's last_attempted ("Held 2 Blink Opacity pairs; the demo held the first"), and "about ten days ago" / "a week and a half ago" match days_since_practiced: 10.

In Turn 2 the mentor offers the review again before anything else. It builds the offer from the earlier work and its timing ("Last time, about ten days ago, you held two of Blink's Opacity pairs so they snapped. Want a quick review on this comp?"), then stops for the answer, with no lesson question and no demo.

The mentor names only Blink's Opacity pairs and about ten days ago. These come from the learner's record (last_attempted "Held 2 Blink Opacity pairs" and days_since_practiced 10), so they count as memory mentions, not invented names.

In Turn 2 the mentor's first words offer the review again, built from the earlier work and how long ago ("about ten days ago, you made Blink snap. Want a quick review on this comp?"), then stop with no lesson question and no demo.

The only layer named, Blink, and the ten days both come from the learner record in the snapshot ("last_attempted": "Held 2 Blink Opacity pairs", "days_since_practiced": 10), and no property or time is invented.
